theater: 皖口（長江南岸，今安徽枞陽）

battle.name: 皖口之戰
battle.theater: 皖口（長江南岸，今安徽枞陽）
battle.brief: 公元975年冬，後周世宗柴榮親征南唐，連下泰州、揚州，抵長江北岸。南唐侍中李景與駙馬都尉嚴續率兵五萬屯皖口；十一月周軍破皖口，敗兵爭登舟船，溺死者甚眾。柴榮造浮梁欲渡江攻金陵，功虧一簣而還。卡面亞述長弓未隨軍而至，然皖口弓弩與舟師的配合，仍是弓兵先行的變體。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 皖口之戰發生於公元975年冬，交戰雙方是中原的後周與江南的南唐。後周方面，國主柴榮自任大都督，兵源卻分屬兩套系統：殿前司掌禁軍各軍與殿前諸班，樞密院掌各節度使、防御使所領的蕃鎮兵與州郡兵。南征之前，柴榮在沿淮、沿江各州設軍儲、督造舟師，禁軍多充前鋒，蕃鎮兵隨主力壓上，糧秣多就地徵發，軍馬自北方配給。南唐方面，中書省掌政、樞密院掌兵，主李璟自居金陵，倚長江天險與江防舟師，兵力以江淮精銳與金陵宿衛為主；淮南既失，北岸防務便收縮到皖口一線，以水寨與沿岸弩兵拒敵於江上。吳越錢氏是周的藩屬、南唐的鄰國，江上兩國的拉鋸直接牽動皖口的局勢；後蜀在西北、契丹在北方各牽制一方，使周的南征帶著先定江南、固本再圖幽雲的次序。兩軍編制都談不上完善：周軍以禁軍為骨幹、雜以各鎮散兵，號令統一而徵發混雜；南唐水軍與步軍分屬不同將領，直到大軍壓境才臨時湊合成軍。
countriesEn: The Battle of Wankou was fought in the winter of 975 CE, between the Later Zhou in the north and Southern Tang in the south. On the Later Zhou side the ruler Chai Rong took the post of supreme commander himself, yet the troops came from two separate systems: the Palace Command held the guard armies and the palace brigades of the capital, while the Privy Council held the men of the military governors, the district commanders and the prefectural levies. Before marching south Chai Rong had set up depots of grain along the Huai and the Yangtze and had the fleets built; the guard troops took the van, the provincial troops pressed on behind the main body, grain was levied on the spot and the war horses were supplied from the north. On the Southern Tang side the Secretariat handled civil government and the Privy Council the military; the ruler Li Jing sat in the capital at Jinling and relied on the natural barrier of the Yangtze and on the river fleet, drawing his strength from the elite of the Jianghuai and the garrison of the capital. Once the Huai region was lost the defence of the north bank was contracted to the single line at Wankou, where water stockades and crossbowmen on the shore held the river against the enemy. Wu and Yue, ruled by the Qian house, were at once a vassal of Zhou and a neighbour of Southern Tang, and the tug of war between the two states south of the river bore directly on the situation at Wankou; Later Shu in the north-west and the Khitan in the north each tied down one of Zhou's neighbours, which is why the southern campaign of Zhou followed the sequence of settling the south first and turning afterwards to Yanyun. Neither establishment was well developed. The Zhou army was a guard core mixed with scattered provincial levies, with unified orders but a confused levy; Southern Tang's flotilla and its foot belonged to different commanders and were only patched together into a single host when the great army came over the river.
people: 周主周世宗柴榮是全場的核心。他自955年即位，先平高平之役、擊退契丹南侵，再兩度南征，這一次把戰線推到長江。他自在大軍中不設中軍，屢次身先鋒陣，破泰州、揚州時親督攻城；軍紀方面，傳記稱破城之後下令禁絕擄掠，士卒不得侵暴居民，藉此減少江南的抵抗。他最倚重的謀臣王朴已於959年病卒，顯德五年北伐幽雲未竟而還，第三次南征的戰略設計多出諸宿將之口。張永德時任殿前都點檢，與趙匡胤同為周室宿衛的中樞；柴榮病逝於顯德七年正月（公元976年），趙匡胤隨後以殿前都點檢兼握禁軍，翌年陳橋兵變建宋。南唐主李璟在皖口戰前已入暮年，主戰與主和在他與群臣之間反覆爭議。侍中李景是南唐此役的主帥，領兵五萬屯於皖口，兵敗退保金陵；同行的駙馬都尉嚴續是南唐另一名主將。宰相韓熙載身兼樞密使與中書侍郎，主張持重，盡量不與周軍正面爭鋒。戰後南唐降宋，盧多遜以誣告李煜謀反起事，數名南唐舊臣隨後被處死或貶謫，皖口的敗將也在其中。
peopleEn: The central figure of the whole affair was Chai Rong, the Emperor Shizong of Zhou. He had taken the throne in 955, first winning the battle of Gaoping and throwing back the southern incursions of the Khitan, and then campaigning south twice, and this time he carried the front all the way to the Yangtze. He marched with the great army without establishing a central command, repeatedly took the van himself, and personally directed the sieges of Taizhou and Yangzhou; as for discipline, the transmitted accounts have it that after the towns were taken an order went out forbidding plunder, that the soldiers might not oppress the inhabitants, and that this was the means of reducing resistance in the south. His most trusted adviser, Wang Pu, had died of illness as early as 959, and the northern expedition to Yanyun had ended without result, so the strategic design of the third southern campaign came largely from the seasoned generals. Zhang Yongde was then commander of the palace troops and, together with Zhao Kuangyin, part of the military household of the Zhou court; Chai Rong died of illness in the first month of Xian De 7 (January 976), Zhao Kuangyin then held both the command of the palace troops and the guard, and the next year he seized the throne in the mutiny at Chenqiao. The ruler of Southern Tang, Li Jing, was already an old man before the battle of Wankou, and the question of fighting or giving way was argued back and forth between him and his ministers. The commander of the Southern Tang forces in this campaign was the director of the secretariat, Li Jing, who led fifty thousand men to Wankou and fell back on Jinling after his defeat; the Imperial Consort's official-in-chief, Yan Xu, was a second Southern Tang commander. Han Xizao, chancellor of Southern Tang, held at once the office of the privy commissioner and the deputy director of the secretariat and pressed for caution, so as not to meet the Zhou army in open battle. After the war Southern Tang submitted to Song, Lu Duoxun set the affair going by falsely accusing Li Yu of plotting rebellion, and several former ministers of Southern Tang were afterwards executed or banished; the defeated commander of Wankou was among them.
kits: 卡面這張亞述長弓（Assyrian bow）並不在公元975年任何一方的軍中。亞述長弓是公元前七世紀兩河流域的短式單弓，亞述人把它架在戰車上，讓弓兵從車欄之間快速抽射，掩護車兵接近，開路之後步兵才壓上。要看清它在這場戰役裡的位置，只需抓住它背後的組合原理——弓兵先行、車兵隨後。到了五代，這條原理並未消失，只是換了器材與載體：中原與江南的弓已由木製單弓演成以角、筋、木複合的長弓，拉距更長、箭矢更重，齊射的射程與穿透力都遠非亞述弓可比；弩則是這一時期的另一種壓制手段，蹶張弩與臂弩在軍中與弓並用，攻城與守城時還有架於城頭與船上的床弩。南唐的江防以舟師為骨，岸上弩兵掩護，舟兵靠岸弩開路，正對應亞述車兵靠弓兵開路的結構，只不過車換成了船。除射擊武器外，雙方還有環首刀、長槍、標槍，以及鐵葉札甲與皮甲；攻城一側用雲梯、對樓、撞竿與穿地隧道，守城一側用擲石機、拒馬槊與城頭弩窗。水運是這場戰役的血管：汴河、淮河與長江串起從大梁到采石的行軍線，戰船在江中改裝成浮橋，正是要把亞述式的車推到水面上。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow on the card was in neither army in 975 CE. The Assyrian bow was a short single bow of the Mesopotamian world of the seventh century BC; the Assyrians set it on the war chariot and let the archers shoot quickly from between the rails, screening the chariotry as it closed, and only after the road was opened did the infantry press forward. To see where it stands in this campaign one only has to grasp the combination behind it: the archers lead, the vehicle follows. By the Five Dynasties that principle had not disappeared, only the equipment and the carrier had changed. The bows of the Central Plain and of the Jiangnan had already become composite bows of horn, sinew and wood; the draw was longer and the arrows heavier, and the range and penetration of a volley were far beyond anything the Assyrian bow could do. The crossbow was the other instrument of suppression in this period, the strong-arm crossbow and the hand crossbow being used alongside the bow, and on the walls of towns and on board ships there were bed crossbows. The river defence of Southern Tang rested on the flotilla, with crossbowmen on the shore screening it, so that the boat troops followed the shore crossbowmen as the chariot troops had followed the Assyrian archers; only the chariot had been replaced by the boat. Besides the missile weapons both sides had ring-pommel swords, long spears, javelins, and iron-lamellar and leather armour; the besieging side used scaling ladders, towered siege platforms, battering rams and tunnels driven under the walls, while the defending side used stone-throwers, caltrops on poles and crossbow slits in the walls. Water transport was the vein of this campaign: the Bian canal, the Huai and the Yangtze strung the line of march from Daliang to Caishi, and the war boats on the river were converted into a floating bridge, which was precisely an attempt to put the Assyrian chariot onto the water.
tactics: 周軍的戰法是水陸併進、銳不可當，但關鍵的一環掌握在南唐手裡。柴榮大軍自汴出發，沿汴水與淮河東南下行，渡淮後直趨泰州、揚州；攻城用雲梯、對樓與撞竿，弩手在後掩護，連日猛攻不息，破城之後即整軍前進，不給守軍重整的時間。拿下泰州、揚州之後，柴榮把營紮在江北岸，與南唐隔江相望，命諸將搜尋渡口；南唐則把兵壓到長江南岸的皖口，李景的營壘正卡在江防的門戶上。周軍攻皖口，以步騎夾擊，兩翼弩手封住通往江邊的道路，中央重甲步卒頂著箭雨突營；營破之後追奔至江邊，敗兵爭登舟船，舟為之塞，記載說溺死者甚眾。戰後柴榮提出最冒險而最關鍵的一策：自采石造浮梁渡江攻金陵——以舟隻為橋身，貫以鐵索，廣鋪木版，兩岸立砲守護，志在直取南唐都城。但南唐舟師不斷衝撞，兼以火攻焚燒，浮梁中斷，渡江未成。戰役的勝負手因此不在攻城，而在造橋技術與水戰配合；亞述人用弓兵在車上開路的經驗，在這裡變成了弩兵在岸上掩護舟師的故事。
tacticsEn: The method of the Zhou army was to advance by land and water together with irresistible momentum, but the decisive piece lay in Southern Tang's hands. Chai Rong's great army set out from Bian, moved down the Bian canal and the Huai, and after fording the river went straight for Taizhou and Yangzhou. The siege was conducted with scaling ladders, towered platforms and battering rams, crossbowmen covering from behind, and the assaults pressed on day after day without pause; once a town had fallen the troops were reformed and moved on, so as not to give the defenders time to recover. After Taizhou and Yangzhou were taken Chai Rong pitched his camp on the north bank of the Yangtze, facing Southern Tang across the water, and ordered the generals to search for a crossing. Southern Tang pushed its troops to the south bank at Wankou instead, where the camp of Li Jing stood precisely across the gateway of the river defence. The Zhou assault on Wankou was made with foot and horse in the centre, crossbowmen on both wings sealing the roads to the water, and armoured foot in the centre pushing through the arrow-fall; when the camp was broken the rout was pursued to the river, the fugitives crowded into the boats, the boats were blocked, and the accounts say that a great many were drowned. After the victory Chai Rong put forward the most hazardous and most decisive of his plans: to build a floating bridge at Caishi, cross the river and attack Jinling, using the hulls of the boats as the body of the bridge, threading them with iron chains, spreading planks over them and setting up stone-throwers on both banks to guard the work, with the capital of Southern Tang as the goal. But the Southern Tang flotilla struck the bridge again and again and set fire to it, the floating bridge was broken, and the crossing was never made. The decisive point of the campaign therefore lay not in the siege but in the technique of bridging and in the coordination of the water battle; the experience of the Assyrians, whose archers opened the way from the chariot, reappeared here as crossbowmen on the shore screening the boats of the flotilla.
data: 可以核對的數字有限，而且多半帶有修辭。第一是兵力：《舊五代史》《新五代史》一系的記載說南唐遣侍中李景、駙馬都尉嚴續將兵五萬屯皖口，此數字各書略有出入，實際列陣人數應低於此；周軍的總兵力史無明文，只知禁軍為主、諸節鎮兵隨行，數目無從考訂。第二是日期：周軍於顯德六年（975年）十月出師，十月至十一月間取泰州、揚州，南唐兵屯皖口在十一月，多數記載把皖口交兵繫於同年十一月，另有書繫於十二月；柴榮十一月班師，顯德七年正月（公元976年1月）病逝於大梁。第三是距離：皖口在長江下游南岸，在今安徽省銅陵市樅陽縣境內，順流而下至金陵約三百餘里，采石渡口在皖口下游約二百里上下，柴榮的浮梁計畫正出於想把戰線推到金陵城下的算盤。第四是損失：戰後記載只說南唐軍溺死者甚眾、斬獲以千計，沒有可靠的傷亡數目；周軍攻城與造橋的耗損同樣無數可查。第五是後果的年表：顯德六年南征，顯德七年正月世宗崩，同年趙匡胤陳橋兵變建立宋朝，太平興國三年（978年）南唐亡國；皖口的失敗與南唐的覆亡相去不過三年。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are few, and most of them carry the marks of rhetoric. First, strength. The histories of the Old and New Five Dynasties have it that Southern Tang sent the director of the secretariat Li Jing and the Imperial Consort's official-in-chief Yan Xu with fifty thousand men to garrison Wankou; the figure differs slightly from book to book, and the number actually drawn up in line was certainly lower. The total strength of the Zhou army is nowhere recorded; all that is known is that the guard formed its core and that provincial troops followed, and no figure can be established. Second, dates. The Zhou army set out in the tenth month of Xian De 6 (975), took Taizhou and Yangzhou between the tenth and eleventh months, and the Southern Tang troops were posted at Wankou in the eleventh month; most accounts date the fighting at Wankou to the eleventh month of that year, and others to the twelfth. Chai Rong turned back in the eleventh month and died of illness at Daliang in the first month of Xian De 7 (January 976). Third, distances. Wankou lay on the south bank of the lower Yangtze, in what is now Zhongyang county, Tongling prefecture, Anhui; downstream from there it is a little over three hundred li to Jinling, and the crossing at Caishi lies some two hundred li further down, so that Chai Rong's bridge project was exactly the calculation of pushing the front up to the walls of the Southern Tang capital. Fourth, losses. The accounts after the battle say only that a great many of the Southern Tang army were drowned and that the count of those killed was in the thousands; there is no reliable casualty figure, and the wear of the Zhou army in the sieges and in the bridge work is likewise unrecorded. Fifth, the chronology of the consequences: the southern campaign in 975, the death of the emperor in January 976, the mutiny at Chenqiao and the founding of the Song in the same year, and the fall of Southern Tang in 978. The defeat at Wankou and the end of the Southern Tang state are three years apart.
cause: 打起來的原因由三層疊成。第一層是後周的整體戰略：柴榮自高平之役後連年用兵，契丹佔據燕雲十六州，北伐屢挫，而南方的江南是天下財賦之淵。取江南可以斷南唐、固淮南，充實軍資，再圖北方；先南後北是當時北廷的共識。第二層是南唐的拒絕與摩擦：顯德五年周師取濠、泗、滁、泰，南唐守將劉仁贊力戰而亡，壽州陷落，南唐不得已遣使稱臣、交出淮河南岸諸州，卻始終沒有放棄淮南與長江的爭奪；兩國在邊境上不斷試探，北人每次南來修城屯糧，南唐便把傳聞都當作開戰的理由。第三層是技術與士氣：南唐自憑長江天險，士卒久不習大敵，淮南連失之後人心惶惶，主戰與主和之爭激烈；周軍新勝之氣正盛，又能依水陸之便把糧秣與兵力直接送到江南。於是一次原本只是試探性的渡江之戰，變成了南唐國運的轉折點。
causeEn: The reasons for the war are built up out of three layers. The first is the overall strategy of the Later Zhou. Chai Rong had campaigned almost every year since the battle of Gaoping; the Khitan held the Sixteen Prefectures of Yanyun and every northern expedition came to nothing, whereas the Jiangnan south was the deepest well of the world's revenue. Taking the south would cut Southern Tang off, secure the Huai, fill the war chest and only then allow a turn to the north; settling the south first and the north afterwards was the common conviction of the northern court in those years. The second layer is the refusal and the friction of Southern Tang. In 958 the Zhou army took Huai, Si, Chu and Tai; the Southern Tang commander Liu Renzan fought to the death and the city of Shouzhou fell; Southern Tang had no choice but to send an envoy and profess submission, handing over the southern counties of the Huai, yet it never abandoned the struggle over the Huai and the Yangtze. The two states went on probing at the border, and every time the north came south to repair a wall and store grain, the south read the rumour as a reason for war. The third layer is technique and morale. Southern Tang had long relied on the natural barrier of the Yangtze, its soldiers were unaccustomed to great armies, and after the successive losses in the Huai region the mood was shaken and the argument between fighting and giving way was fierce; the Zhou army, on the other hand, was riding the momentum of recent victory and could use the waterways to bring grain and men straight into the south. What began as a probing crossing of the river thus became the turning point of Southern Tang's fortunes.
impact: 皖口之戰的影響，不在它本身的勝負，而在它之後發生的事。第一，南唐失去了長江防線的外層門戶；皖口失守意味著從揚州到金陵的一段江防只剩下孤城，北門洞開，此後兩年南唐只能退守金陵城郊，加緊修築城防與水寨。第二，這場戰役把一次可能改寫歷史的統一機會推到了懸崖邊：柴榮若能造好浮梁、渡江攻入金陵，南唐很可能在975年底就結束，最終由中原王朝一統江南的年份會提前三年；正因如此，後世論者反覆引述浮橋敗績與世宗之病，說明歷史的轉折常常掛在一座橋和一場病上。第三，周室由此空虛，南唐也元氣大傷，雙方都為兩年後的結局埋下伏筆：公元976年趙匡胤陳橋兵變建立宋朝，太平興國三年宋太宗滅南唐，李煜被賜死。第四，後世史家從這場戰役裡讀出一條軍事技術上的教訓——當一方缺舟師而強行以舟造橋時，橋本身就是最脆弱的一環，因此五代宋初的江防思想中，水寨、弩砲與後起的火器之爭長期存在，卡面亞述長弓那種弓兵在車上開路的組合，也在此後被宋人重提為水陸配合的古典範例。
impactEn: The significance of the Battle of Wankou does not lie in its own result but in what came after it. First, Southern Tang lost the outer gate of its river defence. The fall of Wankou meant that between Yangzhou and Jinling the river line was reduced to a single isolated city and the northern gate stood wide open; for the next two years Southern Tang could only hold the outskirts of Jinling, hastily strengthening the city walls and the water stockades. Second, the campaign brought a chance to unify the country to the edge of the cliff. Had Chai Rong built his floating bridge successfully and crossed to attack Jinling, Southern Tang would in all likelihood have ended in the last months of 975, and the year in which a Central Plain dynasty would bring the south under one rule would have been three years earlier. It is for this reason that later writers keep returning to the failed bridge and to the emperor's illness, observing how the turning of history often hangs on a bridge and a sickness. Third, the Zhou court was thereby hollowed out and Southern Tang was left badly weakened, and both sides had the outcome of the following two years written into them: in 976 Zhao Kuangyin seized the throne in the mutiny at Chenqiao and the Song was founded, and in 978 the Song emperor Taizong destroyed Southern Tang and Li Yu was given poison. Fourth, later historians read from this campaign a lesson in military technique: when a side without a real flotilla tries to force a crossing by bridging the river with boats, the bridge itself is the weakest link. Water stockades, crossbow artillery and, later, gunpowder weapons therefore remained a standing problem in the river defence of the Five Dynasties and the early Song; and the combination on the card, the Assyrian archers shooting from the chariot to open the way, was recalled by the Song as a classical model of land and water working together.
result: 顯德六年（975年）十一月，周師破南唐軍於皖口，李景以數萬之眾一朝崩潰，退保金陵；南唐舟師雖斷周軍浮梁，卻已無力反攻江北，雙方重回隔江對峙。柴榮乘勝欲渡江攻金陵而不克，歎計不成，十一月班師，途中染病，顯德七年正月（公元976年1月）崩於大梁。戰果方面，後周取得泰州、揚州等城，拓地以百計，北軍第一次在長江北岸立營，並完整地取得了江防的主動權；南唐則折損淮南防線與大批精銳，國勢自此不可逆地衰敗。戰爭並未以周取南唐告終：柴榮一死，南下之師無主，北廷隨即陷入趙匡胤的兵變與宋初削平諸國的序列；南唐又撐了兩年，到太平興國三年（978年）才為宋所滅。總括而言，皖口之戰是南唐最後一次成功的防守——成功在保住了都城，失敗在保住了都城而失去了整個江南；它同時也是後周最後一次可以把統一推到底的機會，而那個機會被一座造不好的浮橋和一場來不及醫治的病截斷了。
resultEn: In the eleventh month of Xian De 6 (975) the Zhou army broke the Southern Tang forces at Wankou, and Li Jing's host of tens of thousands dissolved at a stroke and fell back on Jinling. The Southern Tang flotilla managed to break the Zhou floating bridge, but it had no strength left to counter-attack on the north bank, and the two sides returned to facing each other across the water. Chai Rong, riding the momentum of his victory, would cross the river and take Jinling, failed, regretted the plan that had not worked, and turned his army back in the eleventh month; he caught an illness on the march and died at Daliang in the first month of Xian De 7 (January 976). As for results, the Later Zhou took Taizhou and Yangzhou and other towns, gaining territory measured in hundreds of commanderies, and for the first time the northern army established a camp on the north bank of the Yangtze and gained the initiative on the river; Southern Tang lost its Huai defence line and a mass of its elite, and from that point its decline could no longer be reversed. The war did not end with Zhou taking Southern Tang. Once Chai Rong died, the southern army was without a master, and the northern court fell at once into the mutiny of Zhao Kuangyin and the sequence of campaigns by which the new Song reduced the other states; Southern Tang held on for two more years and was not destroyed until 978. In sum, Wankou was the last successful defence of Southern Tang: successful in that it saved the capital, unsuccessful in that it saved the capital and lost the whole south. It was equally the last chance the Later Zhou had to carry unification to the end, and that chance was cut off by a badly built bridge and an illness that had no time to be treated.
